content.title: INSOLVENT | definition in the Cambridge English Dictionary
content.text: Meaning of insolvent in English insolventadjective finance & economics, law specialized us Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /ɪnˈsɑːl.vənt/ uk Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /ɪnˈsɒl.vənt/ Add to word list Add to word list (especially of a company) not having enough money to pay debts, buy goods, etc. Opposite solvent Related word insolvency (Definition of insolvent from the Cambridge Advanced Learner's Dictionary & Thesaurus © Cambridge University Press) insolvent | Intermediate English insolventadjective us Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /ɪnˈsɑl·vənt, -ˈsɔl-/ Add to word list Add to word list (esp. of a company) unable to pay what you owe because you do not have enough money: When it discovered the loans could not be repaid, the bank became insolvent. (Definition of insolvent from the Cambridge Academic Content Dictionary © Cambridge University Press) insolvent | Business English insolventadjective uk Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /ɪnˈsɒlvənt/ us Your browser doesn't support HTML5 audio /-ˈsɑːl-/ Add to word list Add to word list FINANCE, ACCOUNTING, LAW not having enough money to pay debts, buy goods, etc.: be/become/be declared insolvent This May the firm was declared insolvent and its operations were shut down. Currently, companies must be insolvent in order to go into administration. The bank was technically insolvent - it listed assets of $16.5 million and liabilities of $18.5 million. Compare solvent (Definition of insolvent from the Cambridge Business English Dictionary © Cambridge University Press) Examples of insolvent insolvent If they were forced to take what will soon be mark-to-market numbers, they would be insolvent. From Business Insider People even worried some of the world's largest banks were insolvent because of the toxic assets they held. From NPR The company, which began having cash-flow problems in 2010, according to court documents, has since become insolvent and no longer exists. From Philly.com It isn't as if broke is a precise term like insolvent. From NPR Everyone that owns the bonds knows they are insolvent. From Business Insider And all this in an ever more insolvent jurisdiction that every year drives ever more of its productive class to flee its borders. From OCRegister Unless the estate is insolvent, the annual fees for the timeshare will need to be paid from other estate assets, she said. From NJ.com Financially insolvent city-departments and large nonprofits are offered a similarly related transformation -- privatization. From Huffington Post In the insurance industry, state regulators have the authority to appoint a receiver to take control of insolvent carriers. From OregonLive.com With the banks and government insolvent, repudiating the debt and reintroducing the drachma is a winning strategy! From Business Insider She has said her husband's death left her insolvent. From Bloomberg The first thing any insolvent private person is forced to do is relinquish the family silver. From TIME This needs to be carried out for insolvent governments, households, and financial institutions alike. From Slate Magazine Absent reforms, the fund for retired city firefighters would become insolvent in nine years, according to a city report issued two years ago. From Chicago Tribune When you do the quantitative analysis here, you know they are insolvent. From Business Insider These examples are from corpora and from sources on the web.
